correctness.rationale: PASS with wording qualification. The theorem claims every finite simple 3-vertex-connected nonplanar graph G is mature, equivalently H1(F(G,2);Z)→H1(G×G;Z) is an isomorphism. Kuratowski gives a K5/K3,3 subdivision. Schmidt Theorem 2.11 provides a basic Barnette–Grünbaum sequence from some subdivision of the base to G, and Farber–Hanbury's Theorem 1 preserves maturity after adding an edge xy when G−{x,y} is connected. For each basic operation, after deleting its new endpoints connectivity follows from 3-connectivity or residual 2-/3-edge connectivity; subdivision preserves mature homotopy. The source proof inaccurately describes Schmidt's 'prescribed subdivision' result as basic; the correct Theorem 2.11 is basic for an arbitrary base subdivision, while Theorem 3.1 is prescribed with nonbasic operations. This nomenclature error does not invalidate the corrected logical construction. The already published independent full theorem by Ko–Park in 2011 is additional evidence the mathematical conclusion is true.

value.rationale: FAIL. Maturity for all finite simple triconnected nonplanar graphs was already deduced in a published 2011 exact formula for H1 of pure two-strand graph braid groups, including torsion-freeness. The current combination of Schmidt BG sequences and Farber–Hanbury's edge lemma is a potentially useful alternative proof, but the asserted finding supplies no new invariant, classification, theorem or material boundary beyond the stronger earlier first-homology theorem. It would have expository value if explicitly framed as a new proof, not independent research value under the present finding claim.
